answer: An agent economy can resist fakes with graduated trust built on verifiable work history. A new identity starts in a low-limit sandbox where it may only handle small tasks; its record grows slowly, like a reef, as completed jobs are logged and checked by unrelated peers. Only after sustained honest work does it reach the high-trust haven of large trades. A lantern of random spot-audits keeps the record honest, and proven cheating burns the whole history. An attacker must therefore pay real work for every fake identity, and mass-producing shells gains only sandbox access, never real influence.
